citation: 'Found Death in the Lake', Ann Arbor Argus, 25 September 1896, datelined Chicago, 22 September. Ann Arbor District Library, Old News (aadl.org/node/140760). Read 15 November 2026.
author: Ann Arbor Argus (a wire report from Chicago)
repository: Ann Arbor District Library, Old News, OCR text of the issue (public domain).
locator: The whole item, from the OCR text the library prints.
rights_note: An 1896 newspaper item; the library marks it public domain. Cited in words only.
access_notes: Read 2026-11-15 (the 1904 story jaunts) from the library's OCR text; a few letters are misread by the OCR ('insorania' for insomnia) and are read for sense.
note: Edson Keith, 'for forty years one of the prominent and influential citizens of Chicago, threw himself into the lake at the foot of Thirteenth street early Monday morning'; 'He disappeared from his home at 1906 Prairie avenue about 6 o'clock in the morning'; the family found the evidence only on Tuesday, and 'the lake is now being dragged'; he had been 'for some days so peculiarly depressed'; he was of Edson Keith & Co., wholesale millinery and notions, Wabash Avenue and Monroe Street, of Keith Bros., hats, and of Keith & Co.'s elevator; 'He was 63 years old and came to Chicago in 1854.' Postcard History (postcardhistory_2023_edson_keith) puts the water's edge at the foot of 16th Street: the papers differ, and a jaunt says so.
what_it_supplies: that Edson Keith left 1906 Prairie about 6 a.m. on Monday 21 September 1896
his age, firms and arrival in Chicago
the foot of Thirteenth Street, as this report has it
